messages:
Priya: FYI noticed the quota sparklines are misaligned with client-side telemetry for tenant-umbrella.
Noah: concrete example?
Priya: console shows 60s buckets with a big jump at 14:12; py client emits 10s flushes so totals don't line up when we aggregate.
Eli: sounds like sampling_window mismatch. Is the SDK sending any sampling headers?
Priya: yes, header snippet (sanitized):\n``nX-Sampling-Hint: 0.005\nX-Sampling-Window: 10s\n``nConsole ingest uses tenant default 60s.
Sara: we intentionally canonicalize windows server-side to keep cross-client reporting consistent. Problem is we never told the client what we canonicalized to.
Noah: options: (A) server remains authoritative and ignore client hints in dashboard; (B) server returns X-Effective-Sampling-Window in responses and console uses that for bucketing; (C) SDK opt-in to follow server via env flag.
Eli: (B)+(C) seems safest. Server can add header on handshake; SDKs adopt only when opt-in true to avoid surprise.
Priya: can we also add a console-side smoothing rule: merge spikes shorter than half the tenant window to reduce visual noise during rollout?
Sara: yes, quick hack in sparkline aggregator for the short term.
Noah: rollout plan: add header -> staging this week, SDK opt-in flags next week (py/ts/go), console smoothing now. Monitor two weeks then flip default in SDKs.
Priya: I'll collect tenant repros and post before/after screenshots.
